plan.summary: This 4-week opening block is built for off-camp boxing with one S&C session per week, so each session covers the biggest returns first: crisp power work, main strength, then a small amount of trunk and upper-back support. Week 1 establishes training maxes for the primary lift so later percentage work is anchored to your real current level. The main program starts in Week 2, builds through Week 3, and uses Week 4 as a light deload to reduce fatigue while keeping movement quality high.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general lower-body force and whole-body power with simple, repeatable lifting that supports boxing without adding unnecessary fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the main strength work and keep explosive output sharp while holding total volume to a recoverable level.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Shift more emphasis toward faster and sharper power expression while keeping enough strength work to hold onto force qualities.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as possible and land quietly. Reset between reps so every jump stays crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a box height you can land on cleanly without tucking excessively.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Pause briefly at the bottom and drive straight up with full intent.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Rotational Scoop Throw
exercises.notes: Throw hard from the hips with full rotation. Use a non-bouncing ball and reset each rep.

substitutionOptions.name: Medicine Ball Shot-Put Throw

substitutionOptions.name: Half-Kneeling Rotational Throw

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up progressively, then work up to one hard but clean top set. This establishes your baseline for future percentage work, so stop at strong technique.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your training max.
